I had a fruit fly infestation once. There had been a drop of some drink left on a table overnight, and the next morning the surface was crawling with newly spawned flies.

I set up a couple traps by adding some orange juice to some vodka in a small cup, covering the cup tightly with plastic wrap (using a rubber band to seal it), and poking a couple small holes in the center of the plastic cover with a pencil. The flies go in through the hole, but because the holes are poked inward, they can't crawl back out. Alcohol being alcohol, they lose it pretty fast and drown.

Was very effective.

I am a huge proponent of supporting your community and buying local. I have several policies that I encourage others to follow and make your community a better place over time.

  1. Don't shop anywhere that pays slave wages or were the employees always seem unhappy.

  2. If something is a very low price, ask yourself why. Avoid items not sourced in a humane and eco-friendly way if you can.

  3. Vote in your local elections. Don't believe what anyone tells you, it does matter. Some politicians love to underfund infrastructure and services so communities need to actively fight against it.

  4. Start small markets and encourage building owners to not let their buildings sit idle and convince them to make rent affordable. If the rent is affordable, aspiring entrepreneurs will set up shop and they'll be able to weather low traffic and economic downturns.

  5. Don't let crime and drugs root itself in your community. Don't be afraid. Talk to your neighbors. Nosy neighbors are the best security money can't buy. Not everyone lives in a community where the police are reliable so sometimes we have to help each other secure out homes and properties.

  6. Try to produce something. You don't need to hit it big and make millions. Make something your community needs and get rewarded with a little cash or maybe trade with others.

Don't try to do all these at once. Just slowly integrate the philosophy of sustainable communities in your daily life.
